messages:
Marta: Heads up — ACME asked for a header-based escape hatch so their traffic routes to their Dedicated pool for a week of load testing. They want this live by EOW.

Ajay: We need to agree the threat model. A plain header will be spoofed.

Marta: Agreed. Their ask: 'make a way to pin to our dedicated pool from their side without Console changes each time'. Proposal: signed override header + TTL.

Chen: We can't let customers remap to arbitrary internal routes. Signed token + allowlist for which orgs can request overrides. Also record justification and TTL.

Samir: Example header idea (proposal):
```
X-RD-Org-Route-Override: tenant:acme-prod
X-RD-Org-Route-Expires: 1670000000
X-RD-Org-Route-Sig: sha256=BASE64(HMAC(key, org|route|expires))
```
Short and verifiable.

Ajay: Verification pseudocode:
```
payload = f"{org}|{route}|{expires}"
sig = HMAC_SHA256(key=org_signing_key, payload)
if sig == header_sig and now < expires: allow override
else: reject 403
```
We need key storage, rotation, and an ops path to revoke keys.

lisa: Key mgmt: prefer per-org signing keys in KMS (or per-tenant sealing key) rather than a single global secret. If that's heavy, a scoped key per sales customer doable.

ethan: From ops perspective we need: audit events for token generation and verification failures, a revoke button, and a TTL reminder. Can't have exceptions live forever.

ops-bot: reminder: auto-create support ticket if override is active > 14d. :bell:

sec-svc: Security concerns — this must NOT bypass billing/quota checks. Overrides should only affect routing decision, not quota or billing tiers. Also rate-limit escapes must be blocked.

Marta: Good catch. Design rule: routing override can change target pool only; enforcement plane must still consult quotas and per-org rate limits. If override would exceed quota, reject or route to fallback with audit.

ajay: Fallback behavior: if override signature valid but target route unhealthy or at capacity, fallback to default route and log reason. If signature invalid -> 403 + audit event.

chen: Console UX: add "Routing Exceptions" under org settings. Fields: target route (dropdown), TTL, justification, created_by, status, revoke. Console should also produce the signed header token that customers paste into their requests for testing.

lisa: I'll take Console UI + audit events. ETA Wed (prototype).

ajay: I'll add server-side verifier + metrics: routing.override.verify.success, routing.override.verify.fail, routing.override.fallback.count. ETA EOW for feature-flagged rollout.

samir: Telemetry: surface per-org override usage in Console analytics and create alert if override routes exceed 10% of org traffic for >1h.

ethan: Ops runbook: how to revoke and how to force-fallback. Add playbook to eng-oncall.

marta: I'll coordinate with sales/ACME and get their acceptance criteria.

audit-bot: audit:event created: type=override.request id=ovr-1978000000 created_by=marta org=acme reason="load test" ttl=7d

ajay: One more: sign tokens with KMS asymmetric key and include key id in header so verification service can fetch the right public key. That avoids per-org secrets in our DB.

chen: Good call — include X-RD-Org-Route-KeyID: kid-2023-07.

marta: Summary: (1) signed header + TTL (2) console UI to generate tokens + revoke (3) server verify + quotas intact (4) telemetry + audit + runbook. Feature-flag and staged rollout. :+1:

lisa: I'll drop a mock screenshot in #eng-platform-design tomorrow.

ajay: Putting a TODO in the ticket for sec review and KMS integration.

marta: Thanks all — ping me when prototype is up and I'll loop ACME.
